nodes.name: HPNC synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.136 g Zn(NO3)2·6H2O and 1.308 g 2,6-diaminopyridine (DAP) were added into 9 g silica colloid solution (Ludox HS40, 40% in water, Sigma-Aldrich). After drying at 60°C for 24 h, the obtained composites were ball-milled at 200 rpm for 4 h. Then the resulting powder was calcined at 1020°C for 2 h with a ramping rate of 5°C min⁻¹ under flowing nitrogen (0.6 L min⁻¹). The pyrolyzed sample was etched with 10 wt% HF solution (It is worthy to point out that, this step should be conducted in fume hood with extreme caution and appropriate protection due to the high corrosivity and toxicity of 10 wt% HF solution.) to remove the silica templates, followed by centrifuging and washing with water several times. After drying at 60°C for 24 h, the black powder named HPNC was obtained.

nodes.name: Fe-HPNC CVD
nodes.procedure: Chemical vapor deposition (CVD) was employed for the synthesis of Fe-HPNC. Specifically, a certain amount (100, 200, 400 mg) of anhydrous FeCl3 was placed in a porcelain boat in a tube upstream of the nitrogen flow while 100 mg HPNC was evenly placed in another porcelain boat downstream of the nitrogen flow. The gap between two boats was kept 1 cm and the nitrogen flow rate was kept 0.3 L min⁻¹. Then the temperature of the tube furnace was risen to a variety of target values (700, 800, 900 °C) with a ramping rate of 5°C min⁻¹ and held for 3 h. After cooling down to room temperature naturally, the desired Fe-HPNC was obtained.

nodes.name: Co3O4 hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Co3O4 nanoparticles were prepared by a facile hydrothermal reaction. Typically, 127 mg Co2(AC)2·4H2O was dissolved in 40 ml water. Then the solution was stirred at 60°C in oil bath, during which 1 ml NH3·H2O (25 wt%) was added dropwise, and kept stirring for 2 h. After that, the homogeneous mixture was transferred to a 50 ml Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and kept at 150°C for 3 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the dark brown mixture was centrifuged and washed with water several times, then freeze dried, and the fine Co3O4 powder was obtained.

nodes.name: Fe-HPNC/Co3O4 hybridization
nodes.procedure: A certain amount (30, 60, 90 mg) of Fe-HPNC and 30 mg Co3O4 were dispersed in 40 ml water. The resulting dispersion was subjected to an ultrasonic treatment for 1 h and then kept stirring for 12 h. The products were centrifuged and freeze-dried, and Fe-HPNC/Co3O4 with different ratios of Fe-HPNC to Co3O4 was obtained.

nodes.name: RuO2/C impregnation
nodes.procedure: The RuO2/C hybrids was prepared by a facile impregnation-hydrothermal oxidation of RuCl3·nH2O. Typically, 100 mg Vulcan XC-72 was dispersed in 50 ml water by ultrasonication for 1 h. Subsequently, 50 mg RuCl3·nH2O dissolved in 5 mL water was added into the XC-72 dispersion and the pH was adjusted to 10 with 0.1 M NaOH solution. Then the mixture was vigorously stirred for 12 h, followed by centrifuged and washed with water repeatedly to get the precipitate. At last, the precipitate was dried at 60°C for 12 h, followed by ramping the temperature to 200°C and dwelling for 6 h in air.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows disordered spherical pores with average diameter of ca. 12 nm throughout Fe-HPNC; uniform distribution of Co₃O₄ nanoparticles on Fe-HPNC substrates in Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images (Fig. 2a,b) show that there are disordered spherical pores with an average diameter of ca. 12 nm throughout the sample... the uniform distribution of Co₃O₄ nanoparticles on Fe-HPNC substrates is confirmed by TEM for Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ (Fig. 2d and Fig. S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM visualizes single Fe atoms embedded in Fe-HPNC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: single Fe atoms embedded in Fe-HPNC are visualized by aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-STEM) in high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) imaging mode (Fig. 2c and Fig. S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Fe-Nx peaks at 711.1 eV and 724 eV in Fe-HPNC; N 1s fitted to pyridinic N (398.2 eV), Fe-Nx (399 eV), pyrrolic N (399.8 eV), graphitic N (401.2 eV), oxidized N (402.5 eV); Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ shows Co 2p₃/₂ (779.8 eV) and Co 2p₁/₂ (794.8 eV) confirming Co³⁺/Co²⁺ in Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe 2p spectra... show two peaks at around 711.1 eV and 724 eV, attributing to the Fe-Nx configuration... N 1s spectra... can be fitted well with five peaks assigned to pyridinic N (398.2 eV), Fe-Nx (399 eV)... There are two peaks in Co 2p spectra at 794.8 eV and 779.8 eV corresponding to Co 2p₃/₂ and Co 2p₁/₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ and pure Co₃O₄ nanoparticles show characteristic peaks of Co₃O₄; Fe-HPNC-900 and Fe-HPNC-4:1 exhibit sharp peak at 44.7° related to Fe crystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XRD patterns of Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ and pure as-prepared Co₃O₄ nanoparticles show characteristic peaks of Co₃O₄ (Fig. S12, S13)... X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Fig. S11) of Fe-HPNC-900 and Fe-HPNC-4:1 exhibit a sharp peak at around 44.7° related to Fe crystals.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show D band at 1350 cm⁻¹ and G band at 1580 cm⁻¹ with I_D/I_G ratios close to 1 indicating amorphous structures; ratio slightly increases with temperature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two distinct peaks at 1350 and 1580 cm⁻¹ appear in Raman spectra... all the I_D/I_G ratios are close to 1... the I_D/I_G ratio slightly increases with rising temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Fe contents of 0.34, 2.04, 2.84 wt% for Fe-HPNC-x:1 (x=1,2,4); Co content of 7.29 wt% in Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe contents are quantified to be 0.34, 2.04 and 2.84 wt% for Fe-HPNC-x:1 (x=1, 2, 4), respectively... the Co content for Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ was measured to be 7.29 wt%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Synchrotron XAS at Fe K-edge shows positively charged Fe single-atoms; FT-EXAFS primary peak at 1.5 Å (Fe-N), minor peak at 2.6 Å (Fe-C), no Fe-Fe peaks; coordination number ~2 for Fe-N/C confirming FeN₂ configuration in Fe-HPNC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES spectra of Fe K-edge in Fig. 3d show similar near-edge absorption energy of Fe-HPNC and iron phthalocyanine (FePc) while large difference exists between Fe-HPNC and Fe foil... FT EXAFS curve of Fe-HPNC in Fig. 3e presents a primary peak at 1.5Å assigning to the Fe-N scattering paths while a minor peak at 2.6Å attributing to Fe-C coordination. No obvious peaks for Fe-Fe... an average coordination number (C_N) of about 2 was obtained for both C and N.

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ physisorption shows type-I/IV isotherms confirming micropores and mesopores; Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ has BET surface area of 708 m²/g and pore volume of 1.447 cm³/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ still possesses a large BET surface area of 708 m²g⁻¹ and a pore volume of 1.447 cm³g⁻¹... The Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area and total pore volume of all the samples are summarized in Table S1.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms homogeneous distribution of C, N, O, Fe, Co elements in Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping of Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ also confirms the homogeneous dispersion of C, N, O, Fe and Co elements (Fig. 2f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM and SAED confirm crystalline spinel structure of Co₃O₄ nanoparticles in Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image (Fig. 2e) and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (inset in Fig. 2e) show the crystalline spinel structure of Co₃O₄ nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ has the lowest charge transfer resistance (R_ct) compared to HPNC and Pt/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ shows the lowest charge transfer resistance (R_ct) compared with those of HPNC and Pt/C, manifesting a faster charge transfer process.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates gives C_dl of 30 mF cm⁻² for Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ and 29.1 mF cm⁻² for Fe-HPNC indicating high electrochemically active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl of Fe-HPNC/Co₃O₄ (30 mF cm⁻²) is similar to that of Fe-HPNC (29.1 mF cm⁻²) and much larger than those of other catalysts.
